_README: REVIEWED value corrections for docs/sf_revop.json slot 0 (revStd) / slot 1 (revCon).
The revop analogue of fund_cell_fix.json (which does npStd/npCon in sf_fundamentals).
For cells whose stored REVENUE value is simply wrong against the filing itself -- the wrong
line, the wrong period, a mis-parse -- NOT scale errors (scale_fix.json, parse-time).
Every entry states the primary document AND a second independent source, because a restatement
looks exactly like an error until you check whether the later filing agrees. A cell whose
vintages genuinely DISAGREE (an amalgamation/demerger restatement, e.g. SUPRAJIT 2016) is NOT
an error and must NOT be listed here.
Applied by scripts/apply_revop_cell_fix.py --apply, guarded on `was` (idempotent, refuses to
overwrite a cell someone else has moved). Writes BOTH docs/sf_revop.json and the build ledger
scripts/revop_fundamentals.json so the next incremental build_revop keeps the corrected value.
DURABILITY CAVEAT: if a value is reproduced by build_revop's XBRL parse (not just a fill), a
`--fresh` rebuild can regenerate the wrong number. ci_preserve_merge normally keeps the
committed value, but for a permanent fix the XBRL extraction should be corrected too. Each
entry notes whether the wrong value is a scale issue (no -- use scale_fix) or a wrong-line pick.

fixes.why: L&T Finance Holdings std Q4FY19 'Total revenue from operations'. THREE-way proof it is 303.15, not 3.09: (1) the company's OWN Sep-2019 filing (BSE ann 2019-10-18), page 13 'STATEMENT OF STANDALONE FINANCIAL RESULTS ... SEPTEMBER 30, 2019' (Rs in Crore), Year-ended-31-March-2019 column, row (I) Total revenue from operations = 482.11; our three OTHER FY2019 quarters (Jun-18 32.38, Sep-18 97.71, Dec-18 48.87 = 178.96) each equal that filing's own quarter columns, so Q4 = 482.11 - 178.96 = 303.15. (2) Moneycontrol standalone rev_ops for 20190331 = 303.14. (3) our stored series matches MC standalone EXACTLY on the surrounding quarters (48.87, 29.21, 400.49), so only this one cell is out. NOT a restatement (no vintage shows 3.09) and NOT a clean power-of-ten (303.15/3.09 = 98.1, so scale_fix does not apply) -- an isolated wrong value.
fixes.wrong_value_class: wrong-line/mis-parse (NOT scale); if XBRL-sourced the extraction picked a component line, needs a parser check for a permanent fix
